transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You make a great deal of noise for a creature made of mud. My head is already thrumming with echoes from the deep, and I do not need more. Why are you scratching at my gate?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm looking for my brother Omar.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: They all have names when they arrive, but the dark eats names first. Go back up, boy. The air down here is too heavy for your lungs today.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I can't go back without him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You say that now, but persistence is often just a lack of imagination. You cannot imagine what waits in the tunnels. It would be kinder to leave him to the silence.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He's scared of the dark, so he needs me.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Fear is the only honest thing in this pit. My father feasts on fear—or perhaps he simply ignores it now. I can never tell the difference anymore.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is your father the one who took him?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: My father takes everything eventually. He rules from far below and the weight of that reaches all the way up here. You should not ask about him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You sound sad when you talk about him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Sadness is for surface dwellers who have time to weep. I am not sad, little mud-thing. I am simply... full of noise.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I can be quiet if you let me pass.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: It is not the noise of the air that troubles me, but the shaking of the ground. My father is restless today, and the whole kingdom trembles with him. Your silence cannot repair a broken foundation.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is he the one who broke it?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: He breaks many things without noticing, like a giant walking through spiderwebs. He forgets that some webs hold the ceiling up. I am the one who must weave them back together before the stones fall.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You must be very strong to fix a ceiling.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Strength has little to do with it. It is endurance. I stand here and hold the gate because if I walk away, the rot spreads upward. You look at me as if you understand—but you cannot.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have to fix things I didn't break all the time.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Do you? You are a child of dirt and sunlight—what could you know of centuries of maintenance? Yet... there is no lie in your face.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My brother breaks things, and I have to put them back together.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So you follow behind him with a broom and a dustpan, sweeping up the shards. A thankless task. Does he ever thank you?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't do it for thanks.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then you are either a fool or a martyr—and we eat both down here. But today... today such devotion leaves a bitter taste.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not a martyr. I'm just Salim.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Just Salim. It must be a luxury to be so small that you fit inside a single word. I am the Keeper of the Threshold, the Daughter of the Red King, and the Weight of the Mountain.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Don't you have a name that's just yours?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: If I ever did, it was buried under the pile of titles my father placed upon me. He builds his kingdom from heavy words and stone, and I am buried beneath both.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Does he know he buried you?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: He knows only what serves his domain. I am the gate and the threshold and the guardian, and that is all I am allowed to be. The shaking you feel in the floor right now is his restlessness, not mine.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: But you're the one still standing.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I am always the one still standing. That is not a comfort—it is a sentence.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I know what that feels like. When Omar gets in trouble, I'm always the one left standing in front of my mother explaining it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You compare a mother's disappointment to the weight of a kingdom?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: No. I just mean I know what it feels like to be the one who holds things together when no one notices you're doing it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You should sit down and rest.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Rest is for things that die. If I sit, the gate closes, the tunnels collapse, and the order of the world unravels. I cannot sit.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I can stand with you for a bit.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You would be crushed instantly. You are soft and filled with blood, and yet you offer to shoulder a burden that cracks granite.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm stronger than I look.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Strength here is not muscle; it is the refusal to break. If I leaned on you, you would snap like dry wood. Do not pretend we are the same.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I know we're not the same, but I know what heavy feels like.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Perhaps you carry a pebble or two and call it a mountain. Still, that little heaviness has kept you standing where others would have fled.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I can't flee until I have Omar.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That name again, spoken like a charm that solves nothing. You are not a warrior—just a creature who refuses to release what is his.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Does that mean you'll let me inside?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: It means I am tired of blocking your path. Go through before I remember I had a reason to keep it shut.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm going.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Do not look back at me.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I hope the ceiling holds.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: It always does.
